hints: Integrate acceleration $a = 36 - 6t$ to find the velocity function $v(t) = 36t - 3t^2 + c$.
Substitute $t = 2$ and $v = 27$ to determine the constant of integration $c = -33$.
Set $v(t) = 0$ and solve $-3t^2 + 36t - 33 = 0$ by dividing by $-3$ and factorising $(t - 1)(t - 11) = 0$.
walkthrough:
Integrate the acceleration function to determine velocity:
$$v = \int (36 - 6t)\,dt = 36t - 3t^2 + c$$

Use the boundary condition $v(2) = 27\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to find constant $c$:
$$27 = 36(2) - 3(2^2) + c = 72 - 12 + c = 60 + c$$
$$c = 27 - 60 = -33 \implies v(t) = -3t^2 + 36t - 33$$

Set $v(t) = 0$ for instantaneous rest and solve:
$$-3t^2 + 36t - 33 = 0$$
$$t^2 - 12t + 11 = 0$$
$$(t - 1)(t - 11) = 0 \implies t = 1\text{ s}\quad \text{and}\quad t = 11\text{ s}$$

ai_rubric.Integrating Motion Functions: Integrates to v = 36t - 3t^2 - 33 and solves -3t^2 + 36t - 33 = 0 to get t = 1 s, t = 11 s.

teacher_walkthrough:
Relate velocity to acceleration: velocity is the indefinite integral of acceleration with respect to time:
$$v(t) = \int a(t)\,dt$$

Integrate the linear acceleration $a = 36 - 6t$:
$$v(t) = \int (36 - 6t)\,dt = 36t - \frac{6}{2}t^2 + c = 36t - 3t^2 + c$$

Set the velocity function to zero to find the times of instantaneous rest:
$$-3t^2 + 36t - 33 = 0$$

Divide through by $-3$ to simplify the quadratic:
$$t^2 - 12t + 11 = 0$$

Factorise the quadratic expression:
$$(t - 1)(t - 11) = 0$$
$$t = 1\text{ s}\quad \text{and}\quad t = 11\text{ s}$$

hints: Notice that the particle changes direction at the turning points $t = 1\text{ s}$ and $t = 11\text{ s}$.
Split the motion into three intervals: $[0, 1]$, $[1, 11]$, and $[11, 12]$.
Find the displacement function $s(t) = 18t^2 - t^3 - 33t$, and calculate $s(0) = 0$, $s(1) = -16$, $s(11) = 484$, and $s(12) = 468$.
walkthrough:
Identify that the particle reverses direction at $t = 1\text{ s}$ and $t = 11\text{ s}$, requiring integration across three intervals:
$$[0, 1],\quad [1, 11],\quad [11, 12]$$

Integrate velocity to obtain the displacement function:
$$s(t) = \int (-3t^2 + 36t - 33)\,dt = -t^3 + 18t^2 - 33t$$

Calculate the total distance travelled:
$$\text{Distance} = |s(1) - s(0)| + |s(11) - s(1)| + |s(12) - s(11)|$$
$$\text{Distance} = |-16| + |484 - (-16)| + |468 - 484| = 16 + 500 + 16 = 532\text{ m}$$
